### Summary

This section keeps the selector of the lateral covariance correction and the registered arms that exercise it.
The identity behind the correction, the face moments and the telescoping argument are in @sec-ch04-fluxcov and are
not repeated here. At the pin the selector is the deck key `dynamics/flux-covariance`, default true. A deck that
leaves the key out gets the correction, and the key is read per block, so arms with different values can run in one
process. The schema requires every block of a run to make the same choice: otherwise the shared faces stop being
single-valued. Blocks built from one deck do.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Selects the lateral correction of @eq-ch04-fluxcov-dF.

**Data.** Face states and radial moments in; hydro and tracer flux corrections out.

**Placement.** Each lateral flux and its matching geometric source, every stage.

**Activation.** `dynamics/flux-covariance`, default `true`; `false` disables it.

**Guarantee / limits.** Leading $O(\Delta x_1^2)$ correction; no fourth-order guarantee.

**Evidence.** Tests below, @tbl-ch12-flux-covariance-tests; solver ctests were not run.
:::

Local symbols: $\Delta x_1$ is the radial cell width [m]; the face correction has the units of its flux row.

### Derivation

See @sec-ch04-fluxcov for the covariance identity, the face centroid term and the exact telescoping of a shared
face flux. The chapter's check line `[C4]` re-derives the linear covariance identity, the mass-weighted mean
and the two-cell cancellation independently [check `src/snapy_report/ch12/checks/configuration_check.py`, output
`src/snapy_report/ch12/checks/configuration_check.out`].

### Numerical method

`HydroImpl::flux_covariance` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.hpp HydroImpl::flux_covariance >}}) returns the block's
option. On each hydro call, `HydroImpl::forward` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}) runs
each lateral direction with more than one cell through its sweep. With the key on, a hook before the Riemann solve
builds the correction from the face states with `_flux_covariance`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::_flux_covariance >}}), and the correction is added to that
direction's flux after the solve. A disabled direction supplies no corrected flux. `_flux_covariance` gives no
correction with fewer than three $x_1$ cells or a shallow-water EOS.

The geometric source of a corrected direction uses the pressure shifted by the centroid term. A grid whose face
centroid shift is identically zero (Cartesian) keeps the plain source. A passive scalar gets the tracer row of a
hydro species with the same mass fraction through `scalar_flux_covariance`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::scalar_flux_covariance >}}), consumed in `ScalarImpl::forward`
({{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}}). With a correction applied, the species donor limiter of
@sec-ch08 runs even when the EOS limiter is off.

In FP32, the gauged horizontal sweep keeps its FP32 perturbation path only with the key off. With it on, the face
states go back to FP64 totals, because the covariance consumers need totals (`reconstruct_faces`,
{{< code src/hydro/sweep.cpp reconstruct_faces >}}).

### Code

**How to use it.** Leave `flux-covariance` out of the `dynamics` block for its default, or set it explicitly; set
it `false` for the control. In a complete multidimensional card, this fragment keeps both lateral flux directions
active, which the correction needs:

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `disable-flux-x2`[^rg-8a0da0d80715], `disable-flux-x3`[^rg-527913df4a33].
```yaml
dynamics:
  disable-flux-x2: false
  disable-flux-x3: false
```

There is no setup refusal for an unavailable covariance stencil: fewer than three radial cells or a shallow-water
state give no correction.

`HydroImpl::forward` ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}) contains this selection step:

```cpp
    if (flux_covariance()) {
      covariance = [&](torch::Tensor const& wlr, int dim) {
        auto [cwl, cwr] = x1_seam_rows(wlr[ILT], wlr[IRT], dir.seam_tag);
        dcov = _flux_covariance(cwl, cwr, dim);
```

`dcov` is the additive face term of @eq-ch04-fluxcov-dF, built from the face states before the solver may project
them into the face-local frame. The sweep adds it to the computed flux and reports whether the direction was
corrected (`cov2`, `cov3`), which gates the source. The shared-face cancellation checked by `[C4]` requires both
cells to use that same flux.

| correction | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::_flux_covariance >}} | `_flux_covariance` | `dynamics/flux-covariance` |
| apply and source | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `cov2` | `dynamics/flux-covariance` |
| scalar row | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::scalar_flux_covariance >}} | `scalar_flux_covariance` | `dynamics/flux-covariance` |

: Implementation sites for the flux-covariance selector. {#tbl-ch12-flux-covariance-code}

1. Read the key per block, on unless set false. The anchor `flux_covariance` is in
   {{< code src/hydro/hydro.hpp HydroImpl::flux_covariance >}}.
2. For each lateral direction, build the correction from the face states, add it to the flux, and correct that
   direction's source. The anchor `cov2` is in {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}.
3. Give each passive scalar its own tracer row from the same face states. The anchor `cov` is in
   {{< code src/scalar/scalar.cpp ScalarImpl::forward >}}.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The correction is $O(\Delta x_1^2)$. No test fits its order. Nothing at setup checks that the blocks of a run agree
on the key: blocks built from one deck agree, and blocks built separately in Python are the caller's
responsibility. Across MPI ranks the correction has no registered evidence beyond the $x_1$-split and cubed-sphere
tests above.

The complete switch inventory is @sec-ch12-matrix.
:::
